Codex: ii + 6 + 1, i, 148, ii, 147, ii, 1, i, 1, ii + i + xvi + i + ii leaves. The manuscript opens with eight endleaves, two added to the volume when it was most recently bound and six added when it was bound in the 16th century (see Binding for further details). From that point onwards, the medieval portion of the manuscript begins, however leaves were added in various places during the 16th century in order to supply space for a table of contents, a printed accompaniment to part of the text, or text missing through the loss of leaves. These different leaves have been enumerated above and distinguished from the medieval leaves by commas. The plus sign separates this medieval section from the various endleaves or added leaves that precede or follow it. (See Part 2's Additions for further details of the contents of some of these). Two unfoliated paper stubs are present after f. 21, in place of two excised leaves, and were added in order to secure the binding of the two leaves (ff. 16-17) that were originally conjoint with them. Being stubs rather than partial leaves, they are not included in this statement of extent. However, since one of them does contain a 19th/20th-century annotation in pencil, they have been assigned numbers for the purpose of this digital record (see Foliation).
